sources.citation: Soglo, David. 2015. The structure of the Gichode noun phrase. MPhil thesis, University of Ghana, Legon. xii+105 pp. (118-page PDF). Supervisors P. Agbedor, K. Saah.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. Syntax thesis (noun-phrase structure, pronouns) with no phonology section; 'stress' occurs once as a verb ('stressed by both linguists'), 'tone' and 'accent' 0 hits in the whole text. Background pp. 3-4: 'The only major linguistic work done in Gichode is the translation of the Bible by.. (GILLBT) and a comparative study of the wordlist of this Guan language group by Snider (1989).'

sources.citation: Diller, Jason & Kari Jordan-Diller. 2008. Ginyanga literacy development: a survey of attitudes and strategies. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2008-020. 28 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology (sociolinguistic attitude survey). p. 5 sec. 1.3 'Previous Research': 'An unpublished grammatical and phonological analysis of Gikyode was completed by GILLBT members Natalie Sand and Linda Neeley'; also says the Cleal 1977 WALDS Ginyanga sheet 'includes a short word list, phrase list, phonology, and explanation of syllable structure and tone'. downloaded from a 2012 Internet Archive copy of sil.org/silesr/2008/live sil.org is could not be reached by automated download).

sources.citation: Painter, Colin. 1967. The distribution of Guang in Ghana, and a statistical pre-testing of twenty-five idiolects. Journal of West African Languages 4(1): 25-78.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. pp. 27-28 sec. 5 'Transcription' gives tone-marking conventions only: 'High tones will be represented by h, mid tones by m, low by l..'; 'The tones are placed after the word and tone bearing units are separated by hyphens'. Comparative wordlist of 25 Guang idiolects; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Cleal, Alizon M. 1977. Gechode. In M. E. Kropp Dakubu (ed.), West African Language Data Sheets, vol. 1. Legon / Leiden: West African Linguistic Society / Afrika-Studiecentrum.

sources.note: Standard WALDS data sheet with a phonology section (consonants, vowels, syllable structure, tone, per Diller 2008's description of the companion Ginyanga sheet); the most likely printed place for an explicit tone/stress remark on Gikyode. Not online (confirmed by several sibling checks: no archive.org, HathiTrust in-copyright, Google Books no view).

sources.citation: Sand, Natalie. 1997. Descriptive reduplication in Gikyode. Institute of African Studies Research Review 9/10, Supplement 12 (GILLBT Academic Seminar Week: Proceedings of 1995 Seminar): 28-35. Tamale: GILLBT.

sources.note: The only published Gikyode phonology paper; reduplication of descriptive words will mark tone and may discuss prosodic structure. SIL archive 57614 lists it as 'Not Available Online'.

sources.note: Tone-marked Gichode wordlist with an introduction on transcription and the sound systems of the five languages; the source Soglo 2015 names as the only prior linguistic work. SIL archive 3119 has no file; OCLC 24309800.

sources.citation: Sand, Natalie & Linda Neeley. n.d. [c. 1985-2000]. Grammatical and phonological analysis of Gikyode. Unpublished ms., Ghana Institute of Linguistics, Literacy and Bible Translation (GILLBT), Tamale/Nkwanta. Reported in Diller & Jordan-Diller 2008: 5.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only phonological description of Gikyode known to exist; a GILLBT phonology write-up would state the tone system and, in SIL practice, whether stress plays any role. Not in Glottolog, the SIL bibliography, or any repository.
